import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_49/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_49/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_49/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_49/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_49/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_49/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_49/training_6.csv"
]

# Read all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numeric index column
dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in files]

# Union all source tables by concatenation
union_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure columns have correct types as per target schema
union_df['nombre'] = union_df['nombre'].astype(str)
union_df['n_concursados'] = union_df['n_concursados'].astype(int)
union_df['n_aprobados'] = union_df['n_aprobados'].astype(int)
union_df['año'] = union_df['año'].astype(int)

# The target schema and examples indicate no further transformation is needed
# Just save the unioned dataframe as the target output
union_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_49/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
